results.title: Visualizing Inter-Rater Reliability | Bret Staudt Willet
results.content: Qualitative studies often report inter-reliability (IRR) scores as a measure of the trustworthiness of coding, or an assurance to readers that they might follow the researcher’s codebook and expect to find similar results. Reporting kappa scores assures readers that in the instances when a rare code is used, the codebook is clear enough that a second coder will catch it. Of course, the whole qualitative coding process can be tricky, and in many cases, researchers must go through multiple rounds of dual coding a sample, revising the codebook, and coding a new sample. ## Visualization: Inter-rater Reliability Scores Plotted Across Five Rounds of Dual Coding. *Note.* In my research, I follow a rule of thumb where two independent coders apply the codebook to 10% of the corpus in distinct rounds of coding until percent agreement on all codes is above 0.80 (i.e., 80%) and Cohen’s kappa for all codes is above 0.60.

results.title: What is Inter-rater Reliability: Definition, Cohen’s Kappa & more
results.content: Understand inter-rater reliability, Cohen's Kappa, ICC, rate training and percentage agreement. Inter-rater reliability (IRR) measures how consistently different individuals, or labelers, agree on a task. Inter-rater reliability measures how often two or more people (also known as raters) agree when labeling, rating, or reviewing the same content. In Vision AI, inter-rater reliability is a key part of the data labeling process. * **Inter-rater reliability:** Inter-rater reliability looks at how much agreement there is between different people performing the same task. ## Measures of inter-rater reliability. Another way to measure inter-rater reliability is percent agreement, which calculates the percentage of times raters make the same decision. Inter-rater reliability helps teams dealing with such data evaluate how consistent expert judgments really are. Inter-rater reliability makes it possible for teams to check whether those labels are being applied the same way across annotators. Inter-rater reliability measures how consistently people apply labels or make decisions.

results.title: Mastering Inter-Rater Reliability in SLP Research
results.content: Inter-rater reliability is a crucial aspect of research in speech-language pathology (SLP) as it ensures that the findings are credible and generalizable. In SLP research, inter-rater reliability is essential to establish the consistency and accuracy of assessment tools, diagnostic criteria, and treatment outcomes 1. ### Types of Inter-Rater Reliability: Absolute Agreement and Relative Consistency. ### Methods for Assessing Inter-Rater Reliability: Cohen's Kappa and Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC). Two commonly used statistical methods for assessing inter-rater reliability are Cohen's kappa and intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). In this section, we will discuss strategies for improving inter-rater reliability, including rater training and calibration, clear definition of rating criteria and protocols, and use of standardized assessment tools and measures. results.title: Inter-coder reliability: pros, cons and alternatives
results.content: # Should you use inter-rater reliability in qualitative coding? With complex data sets, and ‘wicked’ issues, there are times that a researcher coding qualitative data will not consistently code different sources to the same themes or codes in the same way. This is essentially a triangulation process between different researchers' interpretations and coding of qualitative data. Often, researchers will be asked to quantify the level of agreement between the different codes, looking at how often the coding agrees: that is usually that two (or more) coders have applied the same code to the same section of the data. Cohen’s Kappa and Fleiss’s Kappa are two statistical tests often used in qualitative research to demonstrate a level of agreement. But before qualitative researchers use any method of interrater reliablity, they should understand what they are and how they work.
